citation.title: Diagnostics for plasma control – From ITER to DEMO
citation.authors: W. Biel, R. Albanese, R. Ambrosino, M. Ariola, et al.

topic: Conceptual DEMO diagnostic-and-control suite: robustness, retracted front ends, redundancy, and mapping of diagnostics to control tasks
own_question: Which diagnostic methods and integration approaches could support DEMO flat-top plasma control under nuclear, erosion and space constraints?
actual_method_and_evidence: A design and requirements review, not an empirical study. It contains no CES, no KSTAR data and no nowcasting. Ion temperature appears only as a quantity that neutron spectroscopy (1 s resolution) or gamma spectroscopy could provide. Quoted neutron-camera accuracies are performance assessments, not measured control results.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reactor-oriented control concepts stress reliable diagnostics and combine measurements with control-oriented models, partly because front-end diagnostics may degrade.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a DEMO conceptual requirement and the authors' view, not a demonstrated result. It does not address CES or the timing of temperature reports.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant; no report-latency or nowcasting analysis.
forbidden_inferences: It does not show that a CES nowcast is needed or useful.
It does not establish requirements for KSTAR or for real-time Ti.
It does not show that prior diagnostics are noncausal.
Its redundancy factor of two is a tentative assumption, not a validated value.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most, this could be optional general background on why reactor-oriented control prefers robust, redundant diagnostics combined with models. It is not specific to impurity-ion CES nowcasting and can be omitted.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
